questions.subtopic: Adjective Formation: Consonant + Y Ending
questions.question:
Select the option that correctly completes the sentence:
"This judicial proceeding was ___ than the civil suit concluded last week."

options.text: heavyer
heavier
more heavy
more heavier

questions.explanation: Consonant + 'y' par end hone wale two-syllable adjectives (jaise 'heavy') mein 'y' ko 'i' mein convert karke '-er' lagaya jata hai: h-e-a-v-i-e-r. 'Heavyer' spelling error hai aur 'more heavier' double comparative error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Regular Inflections & CVC Consonant Doubling.
questions.hint: 'Heavy' consonant + y par end hota hai. 'y' kis letter mein convert hota hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Irregular Comparisons: Late / Later / Latter
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate word:
"Between filing a writ petition and submitting an administrative representation, the advocate advised the ___ course of action."

options.text: later
latter
latest
last

questions.explanation: Jab do mentioned entities (1. writ petition, 2. administrative representation) mein se doosri wali entity ki baat ho rahi ho, toh ORDER/POSITION ke liye strictly 'LATTER' use hota hai. 'Later' time (samay) ke liye use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Irregular Adjectives & Suppletive Grading.
questions.hint: Do options mein se doosre (second) option ko kya kehte hain?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Pleonasm Elimination: Double Comparative
questions.question:
Identify the incorrect part of the sentence:
"The new appellate procedure (A) / introduced by the High Court (B) / is more easier to understand (C) / than the earlier guidelines. (D)"

options.text: Part A (The new appellate procedure)
Part B (introduced by the High Court)
Part C (is more easier to understand)
Part D (than the earlier guidelines)

questions.explanation: Part C mein error hai. 'Easy' ka comparative form 'easier' hota hai. 'Easier' ke aage additional 'more' lagana double comparative pleonasm hai. Correct form 'is easier to understand' hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Double Comparative & Superlative Ban (Pleonasm).
questions.hint: Check karein: Kya 'easier' ke pehle 'more' lagna chahiye?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Latin Comparatives: Inferior and Superior with 'TO'
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct preposition:
"The electronic evidence presented by the prosecution was considered inferior ___ the certified forensic report."

options.text: than
to
from
against

questions.explanation: 'Inferior' ek Latin origin ka adjective hai (ending in '-or'). Latin comparatives (superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior) hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karte hain, 'than' nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The Latin Comparative Law: '-OR' Adjectives Take 'TO'.
questions.hint: Latin adjectives ending in '-or' ke baad kaunsa preposition aata hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Two Entities Boundary: Exactly 2 Items Require Comparative
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence when comparing exactly two items:

options.text: Of the two advocates arguing the constitutional matter, Mr. Rao is the most experienced.
Of the two advocates arguing the constitutional matter, Mr. Rao is the more experienced.
Of the two advocates arguing the constitutional matter, Mr. Rao is more experienced than all.
Of the two advocates arguing the constitutional matter, Mr. Rao is most experienced.

questions.explanation: Jab comparison strictly 2 entities ('Of the two advocates...') ke beech ho, toh Superlative degree ('the most experienced') use karna grammatical impossibility hai. Exactly do ke beech superiority dikhane ke liye comparative form ke pehle 'the' lagta hai: 'the more experienced' (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Entity Count Boundaries: Binary (2) vs Group (3+).
questions.hint: Jab strictly 2 logon ki baat ho ('Of the two...'), toh comparative lagta hai ya superlative?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Logical Equivalence: Singular Noun Attribute ('That of')
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"The judicial administration (A) / of Rajasthan is acknowledged (B) / to be more efficient (C) / than any other Indian state. (D)"

options.text: Part A (The judicial administration)
Part B (of Rajasthan is acknowledged)
Part C (to be more efficient)
Part D (than any other Indian state)

questions.explanation: Part D mein error hai. Left side par 'The judicial administration of Rajasthan' compare ho raha hai, lekin Part D mein direct 'any other Indian state' se compare kar diya gaya. Administration ka comparison state se nahi ho sakta; state ke administration se hona chahiye. Correct phrasing: 'than THAT OF any other Indian state'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Logical Equivalence in Comparisons: 'That of' & 'Those of'.
questions.hint: Kya 'administration' ka comparison kisi 'state' se ho sakta hai ya 'state ke administration' se?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Logical Equivalence: Plural Noun Attributes ('Those of')
questions.question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the faulty comparison:
"The judgments delivered by this bench are more comprehensive than the previous bench."

options.text: The judgments delivered by this bench are more comprehensive than that of the previous bench.
The judgments delivered by this bench are more comprehensive than those of the previous bench.
The judgments delivered by this bench are more comprehensive then the previous bench.
The judgments delivered by this bench are comprehensive than the previous bench.

questions.explanation: Subject entity plural noun phrase hai: 'The judgments delivered by this bench'. Right-hand side par previous bench ke judgments se comparison hona chahiye. Plural noun 'judgments' ko substitute karne ke liye plural pronoun 'THOSE OF' lagaya jata hai: 'more comprehensive than those of the previous bench'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Logical Equivalence in Comparisons: 'That of' & 'Those of'.
questions.hint: 'Judgments' plural noun hai. Iske liye 'that of' lagega ya 'those of'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Self-Exclusion Rule: 'Than Any Other'
questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly expresses the comparative degree?

options.text: Gold is more ductile than any metal known to jewelers.
Gold is more ductile than any other metal known to jewelers.
Gold is more ductile than all metal known to jewelers.
Gold is more ductile than other metal known to jewelers.

questions.explanation: Gold khud ek metal hai. Comparative degree mein jab subject usi group ke baaki members se compare ho, toh subject ko group se exclude karne ke liye 'OTHER' lagana compulsory hai: 'than ANY OTHER metal' (Option B). Option A mein 'other' missing hone se Gold khud se compare ho raha hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Group Self-Exclusion: 'Than Any Other + Singular Noun'.
questions.hint: Gold ek metal hai. Kya gold khud se zyada ductile ho sakta hai bina 'other' lagaye?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: 'One of the' Superlative Concord
questions.question: Select the sentence with accurate grammatical concord:

options.text: He is one of the most brilliant scholar who has graduated from the law university.
He is one of the most brilliant scholars who have graduated from the law university.
He is one of the most brilliant scholar who have graduated from the law university.
He is one of the most brilliant scholars who has graduated from the law university.

questions.explanation: Do key rules apply ho rahe hain: (1) 'One of the + superlative' ke baad hamesha PLURAL noun lagta hai ('scholars', NOT scholar); (2) Relative pronoun 'who' ka antecedent plural noun 'scholars' hai, isliye subordinate clause ki verb bhi PLURAL hogi ('who HAVE graduated'). Dono conditions Option B mein flawlessly satisfied hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: The 'One of the' Superlative Concord Formula.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ke baad noun plural hoga ('scholars'). Relative pronoun 'who' ke baad verb kiske hisaab se aayegi?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Adjective vs Adverb: Action Verb Modification
questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly fills in the blank:
"The newly installed high-speed server processed electronic court records ___ than the older system."

options.text: more quick
more quicker
more quickly
most quickly

questions.explanation: Sentence mein action verb 'processed' ke manner ko qualify karna hai. Action verb ko qualify karne ke liye Adverb chahiye ('quickly'). Aur do systems ka comparison 'than' ke sath ho raha hai, isliye comparative adverb 'MORE QUICKLY' use hoga (Option C).
questions.ruleReference: Section 8: Adjectives vs Adverbs in Comparison.
questions.hint: Verb 'processed' ek action hai. Action ko modify karne ke liye adjective chahiye ya adverb?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Correlative Parallel Progression: 'The more..., the more...'
questions.question: Select the grammatically correct correlative comparative sentence:

options.text: Higher you climb the administrative hierarchy, greater the responsibility.
The higher you climb the administrative hierarchy, the greater the responsibility.
The higher you climb the administrative hierarchy, greater the responsibility.
Higher you climb the administrative hierarchy, the greater the responsibility.

questions.explanation: Parallel progression (proportional change) express karne ke liye formula hota hai: 'THE + Comparative ..., THE + Comparative ...'. Dono clauses ke shuru mein definite article 'THE' lagana mandatory hai: 'THE higher you climb..., THE greater the responsibility' (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Parallel Progression: 'The More..., The More...'.
questions.hint: Dono halves mein 'THE + Comparative' hona zaroori hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Intensifiers with Comparative Degree
questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses an intensifier with a comparative adjective?

options.text: Today the network connectivity across district courts is very better.
Today the network connectivity across district courts is much better.
Today the network connectivity across district courts is too better.
Today the network connectivity across district courts is more better.

questions.explanation: Comparative degree ko intensify karne ke liye adverb 'MUCH', 'FAR', ya 'A LOT' use hota hai ('much better'). Adverb 'VERY' strictly positive degree ko modify karta hai ('very good', never *very better). Isliye Option B strictly correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 9: Special Comparison Expressions: Intensifiers.
questions.hint: Comparative degree ke aage 'very' lagta hai ya 'much'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Pronoun Case After 'Than': Subjective vs Objective
questions.question:
In formal competitive examination grammar, select the option that correctly completes the subject-to-subject comparison:
"The senior stenographer types significantly faster than ___."

options.text: me
I
myself
mine

questions.explanation: Formal standard English aur competitive examinations mein jab comparison do grammatical subjects ke beech ho (The stenographer types vs I type), toh 'than' ke baad subjective/nominative pronoun case aata hai: 'faster than I [do]'. Informal spoken English mein 'than me' popular hai, lekin formal exam standards 'than I' ko correct maante hain.
questions.ruleReference: Section 4: Comparative Degree with 'than': Pronoun Cases.
questions.hint: Formal subject-to-subject comparison mein nominative pronoun 'I' lagta hai ya objective 'me'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Sentence Transformation: Unique Apex to Comparative
questions.question:
Transform the following superlative sentence into comparative degree:
"Shakespeare is the greatest English playwright."

options.text: Shakespeare is greater than any English playwright.
Shakespeare is greater than any other English playwright.
Shakespeare is greater than most English playwrights.
Shakespeare is not greater than any other English playwright.

questions.explanation: Unique Apex superlative ('the greatest') ko comparative degree mein transform karne ke liye formula hai: 'Subject + Comparative + than ANY OTHER + Singular Noun'. Shakespeare khud ek English playwright hain, isliye unhe exclude karne ke liye 'any other English playwright' mandatory hai (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.hint: Unique apex comparative transformation mein 'any other + singular noun' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Sentence Transformation: Subset 'One of the' to Positive
questions.question:
Select the correct Positive degree transformation of the sentence:
"Ashoka was one of the greatest Indian kings."

options.text: No other Indian king was as great as Ashoka.
Very few Indian kings were as great as Ashoka.
Ashoka was as great as any Indian king.
Very few Indian king was as great as Ashoka.

questions.explanation: Original sentence 'one of the + superlative' (subset bracket) hai. Subset bracket ko Positive degree mein transform karne ke liye formula hota hai: 'VERY FEW + Plural Noun + were as + Positive + as + Subject'. 'No other' unique apex ke liye hota hai. Option D mein 'king' singular hone se discord hai. Isliye Option B strictly correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.hint: 'One of the' wale sentence ka positive transformation 'No other' se banta hai ya 'Very few' se?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting: Multiple Comparison Violations
questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence containing the grammatical error:
"In the administrative hierarchy, (A) / the newly appointed officer (B) / is much more senior than (C) / his supervisory clerk. (D)"

options.text: Part A (In the administrative hierarchy)
Part B (the newly appointed officer)
Part C (is much more senior than)
Part D (his supervisory clerk)

questions.explanation: Part C mein do serious errors hain: (1) 'Senior' ke aage 'more' nahi lag sakta; (2) Latin comparative 'senior' ke baad 'than' nahi, balki 'TO' lagta hai. Sahi phrase 'is senior to' hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The Latin Comparative Law: '-OR' Adjectives Take 'TO'.
questions.hint: 'Senior' ke aage 'more' lagta hai kya? Aur 'senior' ke baad 'than' lagta hai ya 'to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Two Qualities of the Same Person
questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically free from error?

options.text: The public prosecutor was wiser than brave during the cross-examination.
The public prosecutor was more wise than brave during the cross-examination.
The public prosecutor was more wiser than brave during the cross-examination.
The public prosecutor was wisest than brave during the cross-examination.

questions.explanation: Sentence ek hi public prosecutor ki do qualities compare kar raha hai: 'wise' vs 'brave'. Rule: Jab ek hi entity ki do qualities compare hon, toh '-er' form lagana prohibited hai; hamesha 'MORE + base adjective' use hota hai: 'more wise than brave' (Option B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: Two Qualities of the Same Entity ('More...Than').
questions.hint: Jab ek hi vyakti ki do qualities compare hon, toh '-er' lagta hai ya 'more + base adjective'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Sentence Correction: 'Preferable' and 'TO'
questions.question: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct and standard in formal English:

options.text: Alternative dispute resolution is more preferable than court litigation.
Alternative dispute resolution is preferable than court litigation.
Alternative dispute resolution is preferable to court litigation.
Alternative dispute resolution is more preferable to court litigation.

questions.explanation: 'Preferable' adjective already comparative meaning rakhta hai, isliye iske aage 'more' lagana double comparative error hai. Aur 'preferable' hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karta hai, 'than' nahi. Isliye 'preferable to' (Option C) strictly correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: The 'Prefer...To' and 'Preferable To' Law.
questions.hint: 'Preferable' ke pehle 'more' nahi lagta, aur iske baad 'to' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Preposition in Superlative: 'IN' vs 'OF'
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct pair of prepositions:
"He is the most experienced judicial clerk ___ the registry and the most diligent ___ all staff members."

options.text: of, in
in, of
in, in
of, of

questions.explanation: Superlative degree ke baad prepositions ka specific rule hai: (1) Kisi physical place, institution, organization ya unit ke liye strictly 'IN' lagta hai ('in the registry', 'in India', 'in the court'); (2) Individuals ke set, numbers, ya whole category of members ke liye strictly 'OF' lagta hai ('of all staff members', 'of the three candidates'). Isliye correct pair 'in, of' hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 6: Superlative Degree & Group Comparisons: 'IN' vs 'OF'.
questions.hint: Pehle blank mein institution ('the registry') hai aur doosre blank mein members ('all staff members').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14

questions.subtopic: Sentence Transformation: Reversal with Binary Parity
questions.question:
Choose the correct sentence transformation that preserves the exact meaning of:
"Jaipur is cooler than Jodhpur in winter."

options.text: Jodhpur is as cool as Jaipur in winter.
Jodhpur is not as cool as Jaipur in winter.
Jaipur is not as cool as Jodhpur in winter.
Jodhpur is cooler than Jaipur in winter.

questions.explanation: Original sentence kehta hai ki Jaipur Jodhpur se zyada thanda hai (Jaipur > Jodhpur in cool temperature). Agar Jodhpur ko subject banakar positive degree mein likhein, toh statement hoga: 'Jodhpur Jaipur jitna thanda nahi hai' ➔ 'Jodhpur is not as cool as Jaipur in winter' (Option B). Ye exact truth value aur polarity coordinate karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Section 10: Sentence Transformation Across Degrees While Preserving Meaning.
questions.hint: Agar Jaipur Jodhpur se zyada thanda hai, toh Jodhpur Jaipur jitna thanda nahi hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L14
